decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display stays close to the cardboard core and is cheap to carry, but it has not appeared on the website since 2019 and pandemic retail closures plus soaring paper and energy costs in 2022 push performance below aspiration and invite pruning of overlapping variants.

The standard quarter-pallet display is a staple format at the heart of the one-stop model, so even under cost pressure it is the variant most likely to meet aspirations and be kept despite its absence from the website.

The eighth-pallet format complements the quarter-pallet line for smaller placements at low incremental cost, though its missing web presence and the 2022 cost squeeze raise the chance it is folded into the core range.

The wooden pallet lies outside the cardboard competence, has shown no visible traction since 2019, and with margins under pressure, problemistic search favours redirecting its resources to the core business.

Demand for media-product displays has kept declining structurally, the product has vanished from the website, and the shortfall against aspiration in a cost-pressured year makes withdrawal the boundedly rational choice.
